terminology.petition: Complaint for Divorce / Petition for Divorce
terminology.custody: Primary Residential Parent / Alternate Residential Parent

residencyRequirements.description: At least one spouse must have been a bona fide resident of Tennessee for at least 6 months immediately preceding the filing. There is no separate county residency requirement. The case is filed in the county where the parties last lived together, or where the defendant resides.

waitingPeriod.description: Tennessee has a mandatory waiting period of 60 days from filing if no minor children, or 90 days if there are minor children. TCA 36-4-101(b).

noFault.name: Irreconcilable Differences
noFault.description: Both parties agree the marriage has irreconcilable differences; or parties have lived apart for 2+ years with no minor children

fault.name: Willful Desertion
fault.description: Willful or malicious desertion for one full year without reasonable cause

fault.name: Felony Conviction
fault.description: Conviction of a felony and sentence to confinement in a penitentiary

fault.name: Attempted Murder of Spouse
fault.description: Attempting to take the life of the other spouse by poison or other means

fault.name: Bigamy
fault.description: A prior marriage that has not been dissolved

fault.name: Habitual Drunkenness or Drug Addiction
fault.description: Habitual drunkenness or abuse of narcotic drugs contracted after marriage

fault.name: Impotence
fault.description: Impotence and inability to procreate at the time of marriage

fault.name: Cruel and Inhuman Treatment
fault.description: Cruel and inhuman treatment or conduct toward the spouse as renders cohabitation unsafe

fault.name: Indignities
fault.description: Such indignities as to render the other's position intolerable and force withdrawal

fault.name: Abandonment or Refusal to Provide
fault.description: Abandonment or refusal or neglect to provide for spouse when able to do so

fault.name: Pregnancy by Another
fault.description: Wife was pregnant by another person at the time of the marriage without the husband's knowledge

fault.name: Two-Year Separation
fault.description: The parties have lived apart for two consecutive years with no minor children of the marriage

groundsForDissolution.notes: Tennessee allows both no-fault (irreconcilable differences) and fault grounds. For irreconcilable differences, both parties must agree to the divorce or have been separated for 2+ years with no minor children. Fault may affect alimony awards.

propertyDivision.description: Tennessee divides marital property equitably, considering the duration of the marriage, each party's age, health, earning capacity, financial needs, contributions to the marriage (including homemaking), value of separate property, economic circumstances, and tax consequences.
propertyDivision.separateProperty: Property acquired before marriage, by gift or inheritance during marriage, and pain and suffering awards are separate property and not subject to division.

filingFees.notes: Tennessee filing fees vary significantly by county and whether minor children are involved. Davidson County (Nashville) charges $184.50 without children, $259.50 with children. Some counties (e.g., Shelby County) charge up to $365 including service fees. Fees vary by Circuit Court vs. Chancery Court. Fee waivers are available for qualifying low-income individuals via a Uniform Civil Affidavit of Indigency (TCA 20-12-127).

basic.name: Complaint for Divorce / Petition for Divorce
basic.description: Initiates the divorce proceeding; 'Complaint' for fault, 'Petition' for irreconcilable differences

basic.name: Financial Statement / Income and Expense Statement
basic.description: Mandatory disclosure of income, assets, and debts

basic.name: Final Decree of Divorce
basic.description: Final court order dissolving the marriage

service.name: Summons
service.description: Formal service on defendant/respondent via sheriff or process server

service.name: Acceptance/Waiver of Service
service.notes: Must be signed by respondent and filed with the court

withChildren.name: Permanent Parenting Plan
withChildren.description: Required in all cases with minor children — details residential schedule, decision-making, and child support (TCA 36-6-404)

withChildren.name: Child Support Worksheet
withChildren.description: Income shares calculation per Tennessee Child Support Guidelines

withChildren.name: Child Support Order
withChildren.description: Court order establishing child support obligations

formattingRequirements.notes: Per Tennessee Rules of Civil Procedure

inState.description: Defendant must file an answer within 30 days of service

outOfState.description: Defendant served outside Tennessee must file an answer within 30 days of service

childSupportGuidelines.description: Tennessee uses an income shares model. Both parents' gross incomes are combined and the child support obligation is determined from the Tennessee Child Support Guidelines schedule based on combined adjusted gross income and the number of children.
childSupportGuidelines.notes: The court may deviate from the guidelines if application would be unjust or inappropriate. Parenting time credits may apply based on the number of days with each parent.

alimonyGuidelines.description: Tennessee recognizes four types of alimony: rehabilitative (preferred — to allow education or training), transitional (to adjust to economic consequences), alimony in futuro (long-term periodic — disfavored), and alimony in solido (lump sum). Fault may affect alimony awards. The court considers earning capacity, financial needs, education, marriage duration, age, health, standard of living, and contributions.
alimonyGuidelines.eligibility: Either spouse may be awarded alimony. The court considers the disadvantaged spouse's need and the other spouse's ability to pay.

court.name: Circuit Court or Chancery Court
court.description: Divorce may be filed in either Circuit Court or Chancery Court depending on the county. Some counties have designated which court hears divorce cases.
